text:
sam: Thanks everyone — quick follow-up thread for runtime performance / kernel / batching Qs from today's all-hands. Post any clarifying questions here and I'll loop in owners.

megan: Thanks! First: what's the timeline for the new kernel refactor you demoed? Any risks to Dedicated customers during rollout?

sam: short answer: staged rollout. engineering plans a canary next week (small % traffic), broader staging in ~3 weeks, GA by ~6 weeks assuming no major regressions. Dedicated customers can opt into preview instances; no forced migration.

ashley: Can you clarify the batching/caching prioritization? Is auto-batching still the default on hosted? And what's the plan for prefix/KV cache invalidation semantics?

sam: auto-batching stays default for hosted. Priority order: 1) latency-sensitive routes (no batching), 2) best-effort batching for interactive flows, 3) background/large-batch jobs. For prefix/KV cache: we’re shipping a TTL + explicit invalidation API. Default behavior is prefix-stable caching, TTL 10m, and customers can opt into sticky-KV for session stickiness.

kevin: Saw memory growth on a dedicated pod running 70k tokens/day after last kernel patch. Is that related to the refactor? Any mitigation while we debug?

ashley: pinging eng-runtime — we pushed a GC/kv trim patch yesterday but it's only on canary. For Dedicated you can set env REDWOOD_CACHE_TRIM=on as a temporary mitigation; it runs a periodic KV compaction. Can we get logs from the pod?

kevin: I can share heap profiles. I'll also flip REDWOOD_CACHE_TRIM and report back.

anna: question about quantization support — will the runtime support 4-bit quantization for the bigger models post-refactor?

sam: yes — kernel refactor includes an execution backend abstraction. 4-bit (and mixed int8/4) paths are in the plan. Expect initial q4_xm support in the staging build; full perf tuning after GA. We'll produce benchmark numbers.

megan: for canaries, what's the rollback plan if p95 latency regresses during the canary?

sam: automatic rollback on SLO breach is enabled for canary traffic. We have thresholds: p95 increase >20% or error rate >0.5% triggers an automated rollback and alert to oncall. Manual pause also possible from Console.

ashley: sharing a snippet for a suggested canary config customers can use for preview opt-ins:

```
canary: 
  percent: 5
  slo: 
    p95_ms: 120
    error_rate_pct: 0.3
  fallback_model: "redwood-compat-v1"
```

sam: perfect — we'll add that to the ops playbook.

megan: are there any required client-side changes for customers to benefit from the kernel speedups? Or is it transparent?

sam: mostly transparent. For best results: 1) avoid tiny requests (batch into 64-token chunks where possible), 2) enable streaming so we can stream tokens off GPU earlier, 3) adopt caching headers if you have repeated prefix traffic. We'll publish a short migration guide.

runtime-bot: Deploy scheduled: runtime/canary/2026-11-05T14:00Z -> canary cluster. Owners: @ashley, @kevin. CI: green.

kevin: thanks — I'll watch the canary and post any anomalies here.

sam: thanks all. If you have follow-ups, drop them here and we'll update the public all-hands notes with a short FAQ.
